heading: Risk can fall again beyond interpolation across model classes
definition: across model classes (not only deep networks), risk improves again as capacity grows past the interpolation point, subsuming the classical U-shaped curve.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce a second descent across model classes under specific conditions. Its interpretation as a general extension of the classical U-shaped curve is contested because capacity definitions and training protocols can change or remove it.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for conditional recovery in toy/theoretical settings, with C for capacity-axis and protocol interpretations; R0 for explicitly sized <1B DeiT-Tiny and 1-10B Qwen2.5-7B LoRA recovery results, with C for the tested clean-label and short-budget DeiT-Tiny conditions. Other bucket-wide replication levels are unclear. No explicit 10-100B or >100B coverage: ?.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to V4's general interpretation; conditional occurrence across classes has R2 evidence. Random-projection regression combines high-dimensional asymptotic analysis and simulations showing decreasing bias and variance for m>n, while its isotropic setting lacks the classical first U-shaped regime; reviewed publication status is unverified from the supplied arXiv version (arXiv:2303.01372#R2, arXiv:2303.01372#R3, arXiv:2303.01372#R6). Reviewed MNIST reproductions recover composite tree, boosting and RFF curves, but separating capacity mechanisms gives U/L shapes and moving the mechanism switch changes the peak (arXiv:2310.18988#R1, arXiv:2310.18988#R2, arXiv:2310.18988#R3, arXiv:2310.18988#R4, arXiv:2310.18988#R8, arXiv:2310.18988#R13). Continued weight reuse removes the neural second descent, and changing its switch relocates it (arXiv:2211.10322#r6, arXiv:2211.10322#r7). These provide explicit artifact arguments. Sized LoRA recovery is reported for DeiT-Tiny and Qwen2.5-7B in an under-review study with code, controls and uncertainty (arXiv:2610.04507#R1, arXiv:2610.04507#R6). Its clean-label DeiT-Tiny sweep and short-budget, 20-epoch arm lack a second descent over the sampled ranges; the clean-label curve rises even after training interpolation. These conditions warrant challenges, rather than limits_scope (arXiv:2610.04507#R2, arXiv:2610.04507#R22). Script counts record versions.V4.verdicts.supports.studies=204 and versions.V4.verdicts.challenges.studies=27; these totals precede checker label corrections and do not establish independence. Scale coverage comes from versions.V4.studies_by_size and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.scaling.by_size, which lack 10-100B and >100B keys.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched replications holding the capacity mechanism, initialization, solver and fitting protocol fixed, while directly measuring training interpolation and subsequent test risk, would clarify which contested curves survive. Independent replication of the explicitly sized LoRA results would raise their scale-specific R0 assessment. Explicit larger-model sweeps would address the missing scale coverage.

source.title: Reconciling modern machine-learning practice and the classical bias–variance trade-off
source.authors: Mikhail Belkin; Daniel J. Hsu; Si-Yuan Ma; Soumik Mandal

original_result.setup: The original study varied neural-network size, random-feature dimension and tree-ensemble complexity.
original_result.result: The study found double descent across these model classes, including random-feature experiments with 10,000 training samples. In the tree and boosting experiments, it varied both the complexity of each learner and the number of learners in each ensemble.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.phrase: across model classes (not only deep networks)
wording_issues.issue: The evidence establishes occurrence across classes, rather than a universal outcome within each class. Constant-bandwidth smooth-kernel KRR lacks renewed descent; interpolating dictionary learning rises without recovery over its tested range; a metric-minimizing linear GAN has constant interpolating test error; structured Fourier-character readout loses accuracy beyond its tested threshold.

Some cited results concern narrower mathematical quantities: label-noise-induced excess risk, constrained minimum excess loss, a variance upper bound or an expected-risk upper bound. A singular or declining upper bound does not establish the shape of actual risk; bound-only results leave V4 undetermined.

The evaluation measure matters. Minority-group SVM error can rise while majority error falls; a denoising MSE curve need not appear in classification accuracy; image-quality prediction reports correlation; increasing portfolio relative risk does not establish increasing absolute portfolio risk.

Capacity axes are not interchangeable. Composite learner/ensemble sweeps can show double descent where their isolated axes give U- or L-shaped curves. Increasing convolutional-kernel depth can worsen risk despite interpolation. Nearest-neighbor interpolation weighting and frozen-kernel predictive rank are further distinct axes.

Raw feature or parameter count does not consistently locate the transition. Redundancy shifts it; near-linear random features can peak at input dimension rather than sample count; logistic models use separability; quantum linear regression distinguishes informational completeness from training interpolation.

A sweep may not reach or identify interpolation. Linear random features and functional regression can remain rank-limited; the stated fully trained scalar-output deep linear network has no width interpolation transition; an irrelevant-feature RFM sweep reports a curve without identifying its interpolation point.

wording_issues.phrase: risk improves again as capacity grows
wording_issues.issue: Renewed improvement can occupy a local interval and be followed by another ascent. Basis Pursuit eventually re-ascends; sparse minimum-ℓ1 interpolation has separated descending intervals with an intervening increasing-risk interval; correlated factor regression can rebound as factor SNR declines. These results qualify an interpretation requiring a monotonically decreasing entire tail; V4 itself requires renewed improvement.

Recovery from an interpolation peak does not require beating the best lower-capacity model or a useful baseline. Isotropic minimum-norm regression and noise-predictor regression retain renewed improvement even when lower-capacity solutions are better. LoRA recovery need not regain an earlier valley or dense baseline. Equity-return RFF regression recovers only to the noise floor without beating the historical average. These baseline comparisons do not by themselves contradict V4.

The classical underparameterized U-shaped portion is absent in some supporting settings. Random Gaussian feature selection and isotropic random projections can rise toward interpolation without a first descent. Spiked-covariance OLS starts near optimal and then rises. HMM linear-head theory likewise rises before interpolation. These support a peak and recovery more directly than a complete classical U-shaped segment.

The intervening deterioration or subsequent recovery depends on the fitting procedure. Optimal ridge can produce monotone improvement without a peak. In the one-hidden-layer MNIST network, continued weight reuse removes threshold-associated recovery; when reuse is switched, recovery follows that switch rather than the theoretical threshold. Diffusion RFNN regression retains parameter-wise double descent for finite m>1, while fresh noise as m→∞ removes it. Objective-perturbed Huber regression has infinite limiting estimation error throughout δ>1 after L→∞ and then λ→0 at fixed privacy noise ν>0.

method_sensitivity.factor: Regularization strength, tuning objective and fit tolerance
method_sensitivity.what: For MNIST 3 versus 7 RFF regression (p=784, n=500), λ=10^-7 gives double descent at 2N=n, while λ=10 gives monotone descent; λ=10 is not identified as optimal. Optimal expected-risk ridge makes projected linear-regression risk nonincreasing and substantially mitigates random-feature/CNN peaks. LOOCV- or CV-tuned ridge in fitted-covariate sweeps removes the OLS peak but retains a classical U-shape. These are absent V4 shapes and observed regularization dependence for V6. Positive training-loss tolerance makes the constrained linear-predictor threshold height finite; that threshold-only result cannot determine V4's post-threshold recovery.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training duration, conditioning, privacy and noise resampling
method_sensitivity.what: Finite-time random-feature GD can hide the minimum-norm peak. In the MNIST 0/1 feature-count sweep (n=500, d=784; biased ReLU features; zero initialization; learning rate 1/λmax), the γ=1 singularity becomes visible only for T≥10^8. Feature scaling, initialization, schedules, batch size and solver affect convergence; low learning rates reduce peaks in some settings and eliminate them in others. Diffusion RFNNs retain parameter-wise double descent for finite noise-realization count m>1; m→∞ removes it. In objective-perturbed Huber regression, fixed privacy noise ν>0 yields infinite limiting estimation error for every δ>1 after L→∞ then λ→0, challenging V4 in that condition. Without privacy noise, the δ>1 limit is ε²/(δ−1)+((δ−1)/δ)κ².

method_sensitivity.factor: Composite capacity axes and protocol switches
method_sensitivity.what: Composite tree/boosting axes recover fall-rise-fall curves where isolated learner-capacity and ensemble-size axes yield U/rising and L-shaped curves. In arXiv:2605.21167's MNIST forest (10000 training and 10000 test examples), maximum leaves increase from 1 to 2000 with one tree, then trees increase from 1 to 20 at 2000 maximum leaves. Second descent concerns the combined axis; isolated leaf-only recovery is cannot_determine, so disagreement with arXiv:2310.18988's fixed-ensemble leaf sweep is not established. Moving the mechanism switch relocates or removes the peak. One-hidden-layer networks on 4200 MNIST images worsen when enlarged while retaining trained weights, without threshold-associated recovery; moving the reuse switch relocates recovery to the switch. These shallow-network experiments do not test V1; raw tree-capacity axes do not test V7; switch placement does not test V5's single effective-complexity predictor.

method_sensitivity.factor: Covariance, signal-to-noise ratio, feature scales, rank and baseline usefulness
method_sensitivity.what: Isotropic minimum-norm regression has a decreasing overparameterized tail at low SNR; at higher SNR, risk descends after interpolation to a local minimum and then approaches null risk from below. Both exhibit V4's renewed improvement; eventual ascent does not negate it. Renewed descent can leave a better underparameterized optimum or remain worse than null risk; these comparisons qualify usefulness without challenging V4. For hard-margin SVMs with n=32, isotropic Gaussian features and a 1-sparse signal yield increasing classification error as dimension grows well past interpolation, challenging V4; weak features yield decreasing error. Balanced concatenated random-feature scales yield double descent, while unequal scales introduce additional peaks. Linear-regression variance profiles likewise change a single interpolation peak into multiple descent.

method_sensitivity.factor: Basis, sampling, feature ordering, norm and activation
method_sensitivity.what: Linear ordering of complex-exponential bases produces an interpolation peak at n=N=10 in Cases A and C. Optimal ordering removes that peak in Case C, whose best noisy NMSE occurs at n=10 with slight deterioration thereafter; Case A establishes reduced variance and noisy performance comparable to noise-free performance, without determining peak absence. Whitened Legendre features show spike-and-decay behavior absent from the unwhitened minimum-ℓ2-norm Vandermonde interpolator. Optimal linear activations can remove a ReLU random-feature peak under the stated noiseless regime; empirical per-size activation optimization uses test error. Unweighted Fourier interpolation improves for noise-only targets but worsens for a noiseless single-frequency target. Favorable spectrum-aware weighted constructions establish joint-asymptotic benign overfitting, not fixed-sample capacity recovery.

method_sensitivity.factor: Kernel family, bandwidth schedule, graph structure and input/output scaling
method_sensitivity.what: Decreasing-bandwidth smooth-kernel regression shows recovery where constant-bandwidth KRR does not; Laplace lacks double descent under both schemes, challenging V4 in that condition. Linear-kernel GP predictive loss exhibits the curve where Gaussian-kernel GP loss does not. A one-layer ridge GCN changes from peaked risk at low graph SNR to monotone improvement at high homophily; at graph-signal parameter λ=10, risk decreases monotonically in α, an absent V4 peak and observed V6 noise dependence. Single-hidden-layer hanging-cable surrogates exhibit double descent with logarithmic scaling but no reported second descent with linear scaling; these width sweeps do not test V1's deep-network setting.

Square-loss random-feature classifiers retain peaks in settings where logistic loss removes the noiseless peak, challenging V4; attenuated noisy and real-data peaks remain scope limitations. Relaxing orthonormality constraints and increasing supervision introduces double descent in linear subspace fitting. Random-feature diffusion score matching lacks the recovery found in its regression comparator. Survival-network likelihood formulations differ: PC-Hazard improves past interpolation and supports V4, while DeepSurv's weak recovery limits its scope. Detailed results for Nnet-Survival and N-MTLR report continuing loss increases. PC-Hazard's support does not require its second minimum to beat the classical sweet spot.

method_sensitivity.factor: Risk definition, group metric, capacity measurement and averaging
method_sensitivity.what: Random-design prediction displays double descent where fixed-design prediction becomes constant beyond interpolation. Random-feature SVM minority-group error rises at obtuse angles of 135° and 180° while majority error falls; the minority reversal challenges V4 in that condition. A frozen-kernel predictive-rank curve has a peak and second descent, but does not identify a training-interpolation threshold or establish the same shape on a nominal parameter-count axis. Increasing random-feature ensemble size reduces peaks; infinite averaging yields smooth ridge curves or constant post-threshold logistic curves.

method_sensitivity.factor: Representation estimation, task diversity, synthetic data and clustering
method_sensitivity.what: Perfect covariance knowledge permits improvement with representation dimension where estimated representations have a finite sweet spot. Linear MAML exhibits a later rise at small task diversity/noise but continued descent in reported high-diversity or noisy conditions. Random-projection double descent is reported across tested synthetic-quality settings; the intermediate Pareto-optimal capacity for low-quality synthetic data concerns robustness to model collapse and does not negate V4's recovery. Figure 5 uses n1=300 real and n2=200 synthetic samples, p2=0.4, n=500, d=600, λ=10^-8, with c2=0.0 or 0.1 in the cited rows. TEM clustering produces clearer aggregate-regression double-descent curves than RCM, whose small-cluster-count behavior is unstable.

method_sensitivity.factor: Adaptation family, active feature support and quantum measurement precision
method_sensitivity.what: LoRA outcomes depend on architecture, label noise and training budget: sampled Swin-Tiny interpolating ranks worsen, while other noisy-model sweeps recover. Clean-label DeiT-Tiny and its 20-epoch arm lack a second descent over sampled ranges, challenging V4; clean-label loss continues rising after interpolation. Structured Fourier-character readout continues losing accuracy over its tested post-threshold range, with active support distinguished from nominal band radius. Finite-shot QELM features suppress a secondary peak found with correlated exact features; the extra exact-feature peak does not negate V4's renewed improvement. Quantum linear regression distinguishes informational-completeness and training-interpolation peaks, with training-shot precision affecting them differently.
